$schema_note: Loop 12 C3. The Component Log in .agents/LIFECYCLE.md, made into data so a check can read it. A retirement is any event that ends a name: a component cut, a module renamed, an identifier prefix retired, a flag or subcommand removed, a dependency dropped, a schema field removed. Entries are GLOBAL — one per retired name, not one per referent class — because a class with no registry would otherwise have no entry at all and the record would under-cover silently. allowed_referrers is captured AT RETIREMENT TIME, which is the only moment anyone knows which mentions are deliberate; a correct obituary written then is in the set by construction, a dangling reference appearing later is not.
$historical_note: Records of what WAS. They keep their references by rule rather than by judgement each time. state.json carries decisions[] and SUMMARY.md/INBOX.md are its rendered views, so all three are the same class as DECISIONS.md. Test fixtures are frozen snapshots whose job is to name an old tree. open-brain/docs/ holds dated analysis notes.

retirements.name: enableHeuristicRatings / the heuristic rating arm
retirements.note: IT NEVER RAN. Zero rows across the entire life of the rating_method column — confirmed against the live database, not taken from V-018: 636 rows, 347 pre-column NULL, 267 direct, 22 supplied, 0 heuristic. What it fed was already gone: it produced ratings driving success_rate and maturity, both cut in Loop 10. And the mechanism was this loop's own defect class in production code — it rated an entry helpful when one of its tags appeared as a SUBSTRING of the session summary, which is rule 8 shipped. Leaving it gated off with an honest note would have preserved a live flag with a dead justification forever, in the codebase of the loop that removes exactly that. The `heuristic` value is out of the RatingMethod type and out of RATING_METHODS, so recordFeedbackEvent now coerces a stray caller to `unspecified` rather than minting a value the type no longer has.
